author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Construction is underway to convert the former St. Augustine’s Convent and Paraclete Center in South Boston into affordable housing for older adults. The $15.7 million McDevitt Senior Homes project will create 35 income-restricted apartments and one manager’s unit in the historic building.

The approximately 31,000-square-foot development combines restoration of the existing structure with a five-story rear addition. Plans call for preserving recognizable architectural features while adapting the interior for accessible residences and common areas. The project is intended to add senior housing without removing the property’s long-standing neighborhood identity.

Public financing includes $5.145 million from the City of Boston and Community Preservation Act funds, plus $850,000 from the Federal Home Loan Bank of Boston. Construction began in July, and project partners held a formal groundbreaking on August 20. The reuse adds a relatively small but targeted supply of below-market homes in a city where older residents can face steep housing costs and limited accessible options. Work will now move through the renovation and new-construction phases before residents can occupy the building.
dek: The $15.7 million adaptive-reuse project will preserve the historic property while adding income-restricted apartments for older adults.
headline: Former South Boston convent begins conversion to 35 affordable senior homes
